title: Consumer reports 0.6.1 did not fix docs/log.md clobbering
description: A lore consumer reports log.md still truncating on 0.6.1. NOT reproduced, and deliberately not closed as works-for-me. Evidence against, gathered 2026-09-13 against the PUBLISHED 0.6.1 binary (global install verified byte-identical to the registry tarball, shim removed): (1) worst-case unreachability -- a purpose-built fixture with a 15-entry log across 16 commits, history then replaced by an orphan commit carrying the identical tree so 100 percent of logged commits were unreachable; 15 of 15 carried forward plus the new commit, zero lost; (2) idempotency -- two further syncs byte-identical; (3) CRLF -- log.md rewritten with CRLF, zero lost, so the trailing-CR strip is live in the published bytes. opum-agent independently measured +1/-0 on its own repo and on a clean registry install. Remaining hypotheses, in order: the consumer is not actually running 0.6.1 (different npm prefix, vendored node_modules/.bin/lore, or a session started before the update); a DIFFERENT failure mode being misattributed to LCLI-474; or a shape no fixture has covered. UNCLOSED PLATFORM GAP: only the darwin-arm64 binary was exercised. win32-x64 and win32-arm64 are separately compiled artifacts and CRLF is precisely where they diverge -- the CRLF test simulated CRLF bytes on macOS, which is not the same as the Windows binary on a core.autocrlf=true checkout. Ask the consumer's PLATFORM first; it is one question and it splits the search space.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The consumer platform is known, and if Windows the win32 binary is exercised on a core.autocrlf=true checkout rather than simulated CRLF on macOS
Which lore binary the consumer actually ran is established from their filesystem -- resolved path plus version -- not from npm view
Either a reproducing fixture exists and the defect is fixed, or the report is resolved as not-0.6.1 or as a distinct failure mode with that mode named
If a distinct failure mode, it gets its own task rather than being folded into LCLI-474s record

comments.body:
SESSION HANDOFF 2026-09-13 (session recycled for context budget, not a decision point). This task is the live investigation; the 0.6.1 release it came out of is DONE and needs nothing.

WHAT IS RULED OUT, all measured against the PUBLISHED 0.6.1 binary — global install verified as a real symlink to the npm artifact with the local dev shim removed, so this is not a local build:

  1. Worst-case unreachability. Purpose-built fixture: a 15-entry docs/log.md across 16 commits, history then replaced by an orphan commit carrying the identical tree, so 100% of logged commits were unreachable. This is the repo-recreation shape at full severity, not the two legacy entries the original LCLI-474 fixture used. RESULT: 15 of 15 carried forward plus the new commit = 16. Zero lost.
  2. Idempotency. Two further syncs on that tree: byte-identical output, still 16 entries.
  3. CRLF input. log.md rewritten with CRLF line endings, then synced. Zero lost — the trailing-CR strip is live in the published bytes.

opum-agent independently measured +1 line / -0 on its own repository and on a clean registry install of 0.6.1, and diffed the registry tarball's bin/lore.cjs against the global one (identical).

THE OPEN QUESTION IS THE CONSUMER'S PLATFORM, and it is the single highest-value thing to establish next. Everything above exercised the DARWIN-ARM64 binary only. @opum-ai/lore-win32-x64 and @opum-ai/lore-win32-arm64 are SEPARATELY COMPILED artifacts, and CRLF is precisely the axis on which they diverge — the CRLF test above simulated CRLF bytes on macOS, which is NOT the same as running the Windows binary against a core.autocrlf=true checkout. If the consumer is on Windows, this is untested territory and reproducing it needs a Windows runner. Ask the platform FIRST: it is one question and it splits the search space in half. Requesting a Windows runner is a decision for the user, not something to assume.

REMAINING HYPOTHESES, in the order worth testing: (1) the consumer is not actually running 0.6.1 — a different npm prefix, a vendored node_modules/.bin/lore, or a session started before the update all show old behaviour while `npm view` says 0.6.1; (2) a DIFFERENT failure mode misattributed to LCLI-474 — entries vanishing because they reference commits unreachable after a squash merge or rebase is not the replace-vs-merge bug and 901646cf would not touch it; distinguish by asking WHICH lines survived (newest, oldest, or an arbitrary slice); (3) a shape no fixture has covered.

DO NOT CLOSE THIS AS WORKS-FOR-ME. Failing to reproduce is strictly weaker than knowing it does not happen. opum-agent said the same and was right to.

METHODOLOGICAL TRAP FOUND HERE, worth more than this bug. `git merge-base --is-ancestor abcabb4f v0.6.1` reported the LCLI-474 trailing-CR fix as ABSENT from 0.6.1. That is WRONG — the fix shipped; its branch was SQUASH-merged, so the original commit SHA is not an ancestor even though the change is in the tree. Verified by reading the bytes: `git show v0.6.1:src/core/log.ts` has the strip at line 277. This nearly became a reported root cause, because "CR fix missing" matched the reported symptom exactly. NEVER use --is-ancestor, --contains, or `git cherry` to decide whether a squash-merged change shipped. Read the bytes at the tag:
    git show <tag>:<path> | grep -n '<distinctive line>'

SKILLS THE SUCCESSOR SHOULD REACH FOR: opum-sdlc before branching or landing anything, opum-lore for any docs change (lore check exiting 0 is the definition of done), opum-quest for tracker writes.

STATE: branch chore/LCLI-484-log-report, PR #17 open, tracker-only. Nothing else in flight. LCLI-481, LCLI-482 and LCLI-483 are filed and untouched; LCLI-480 is parked at Blocked on its own branch with PR #12 open and is unrelated to any of tonight's work.
